description: nf-core/rnasplice context, aligned to the pinned 2.0.0 schema. Differential splicing between two named groups.

aligner.help: Alignment route; set it from the question. star_salmon (the 2.0.0 default) also quantifies STAR's transcriptome BAM with Salmon, giving alignment-based transcript abundances beside the pseudo-aligner's; star gives genome alignments only, enough for the event- and exon-level analyses (rMATS, DEXSeq/edgeR exon, LeafCutter, sashimi) and faster.

pseudo_aligner.help: Transcript quantifier (only salmon in 2.0.0); it feeds SUPPA, DEXSeq DTU and IsoformSwitchAnalyzeR.

suppa.help: SUPPA: differential splicing events (exon skipping, alternative 5'/3' sites, intron retention, mutually exclusive exons) and transcript-level dPSI from Salmon abundances. Set from the question: on when it asks which splicing events or isoform proportions change between the conditions (2.0.0 default on).

rmats.help: rMATS: differential splicing events counted from the genome alignments, with junction-read support. Set from the question: on when it asks which specific events change, especially with deep reads and well-annotated events; off for a question only about transcript or gene-level usage (2.0.0 default on). 2.0.0 runs it unpaired unless rmats_paired_stats is set, which Nessie does not offer: the paired model needs the samplesheet ordered by pair.

dexseq_exon.help: DEXSeq differential exon usage: which exon bins are used differently between conditions. Set from the question: on when it asks about exon usage or exon-level changes within genes (2.0.0 default on); it needs at least two replicates per condition.

edger_exon.help: edgeR differential exon usage: a second, faster exon-usage test that complements DEXSeq. Set from the question: on with dexseq_exon when exon usage is the point and an independent method is wanted (2.0.0 default on).

dexseq_dtu.help: DEXSeq differential transcript usage on Salmon abundances (with DRIMSeq filtering and stageR): which transcripts change their share of a gene's expression. Set from the question: on when it asks about isoform or transcript usage (2.0.0 default on).

sashimi_plot.help: MISO sashimi plots: read coverage and junctions drawn per event, for showing or checking specific splicing events. Set from the question: on when the scientist wants to see or validate events; off when only tables are needed, since it adds run time (2.0.0 default on).

isoformswitchanalyzer.help: IsoformSwitchAnalyzeR: isoform switches between conditions and their predicted functional consequences (coding potential, protein domains, NMD sensitivity). Set from the question: on when it asks about isoform switches or what a splicing change does to the protein (2.0.0 default on).

leafcutter.help: LeafCutter: annotation-free intron-excision clusters from split reads, so it also finds unannotated junctions. Set from the question and data: on when it asks about novel or unannotated splicing, intron usage, or the organism's annotation is incomplete (2.0.0 default off).

ignore_tx_version.help: Match transcript IDs without their version suffix (ENST00000335137.1 as ENST00000335137), for a transcript FASTA and a GTF that disagree on versions, such as GENCODE with Ensembl. New in 2.0.0, default off.

contrasts.help: The contrasts CSV naming the groups to compare. The user states the comparison (see required_user_params) and configure_run writes contrasts.csv into the run folder; an absolute path is the user's own file and is passed through.

required_user_params.name: contrasts
required_user_params.definition: Which groups to compare, written TREATMENT vs CONTROL using the 'condition' values in the samplesheet (one comparison per line). Nessie writes the contrasts CSV from it. Which side is the treatment is your call: results are reported as treatment minus control. If you already have a contrasts CSV on Luria, give its full path instead.

pipeline.name: nf-core/rnasplice
pipeline.core_rule: Columns: sample, fastq_1, fastq_2, strandedness, condition. 'condition' groups samples; a contrasts CSV names the comparison. 2.0.0 requires each sample and each compared condition to be an R name (a letter first, then letters, digits, '.' or '_'): Nessie rewrites a UID's hyphens to '_' in the sample column and keeps the UID in nextseek_uid; a condition that is not one is refused.

notes: The comparison is defined by the 'condition' column plus a contrasts file. The user states the comparison and Nessie writes the file (seqera/contrasts.py); the direction is never defaulted. 2.0.0 reports DEXSeq log2 fold changes as treatment over control and SUPPA dPSI as treatment minus control; 1.0.4 reported both the other way round, so results of a 1.0.4 run and a 2.0.0 run of the same contrast have opposite signs. 2.0.0 also removed max_cpus, max_memory and max_time, which Nessie never sends: Luria's luria.config caps each task with process.resourceLimits.

runtime.basis: First guess from typical nf-core runtimes on one 16-CPU Luria node (Nessie's default submit); not yet measured on Luria. Refine from real runs.
